label: keys

events.location: on the white desk, in front of the tablet
on the white hall console, beside the pink cap and a second keyring

notes:
DRAFT -- drafted by Claude from frame-by-frame inspection, NOT yet confirmed in the annotator. Same physical object as VID_20260819_160630_hi: the keyring with the orange/red/purple swirl disc, the dark grey fob and the pale grey strap.
Timeline: handled in both hands from t=1.0 while the wearer walks the flat, set on the white desk at t=11.5, left there while the wearer goes to the kitchen, the hall console and the bedroom (out of shot t=14.5-32.0), the desk is in shot again t=32.5-40.0 with the keyring untouched, picked up off the desk at t=42.5, carried through the kitchen and the hall, and set on the white hall console at t=49.0 where it stays to the end.
Two placements, and they are worth very different amounts. Windows end at t=7, 14, 21, 28, 35, 42, 49, 56 and 61 (trailing), and a window can only report a placement if its LAST frame still shows the object. The desk placement is therefore catchable in exactly one window (the one ending at t=14) -- by t=21 and t=28 the wearer is in the kitchen and truth is silence. The console placement is catchable in three (t=49, 56, 61), because the object stays in view afterwards. That asymmetry is the point of the clip.
The windows ending at t=35 and t=42 are quiet: nothing happens in their span and the keyring is on the desk in their last frame. Together with the three in 160630 that is five quiet windows in the corpus -- still far too few to resolve a false-placement rate, but they are the only samples that measure it at all.
distractor_ids is not empty because of the tail: a second keyring (black round fob, brass keys, white round tag) sits on the hall console right beside this one from t=49 onwards, so the console placement is also an identity test. Identified by appearance as the same keys_02 as in 160630 -- worth confirming.
Boxes are anchored on the frames the scorer actually reads: the last frame of every window the object is visible in (70, 140, 350, 420, 490, 560, 610), plus 35, 130 and 400 as grounding samples. Interpolation between anchors that straddle a hand-to-surface transition (70->130, 420->490) is meaningless, but no window ends there, so nothing is scored against it. On the desk the keyring is 44-95 px on target, below the ~128 px identity floor; the t=35 box is 44 px, which is at chance.
Two calls a reviewer should check. (1) Visibility spans: the keyring sits at or just over the frame edge at 415 (a sliver on the right) and again at 430-435 (in the hand, at the bottom edge, while the wearer crosses the kitchen); I marked all three as in shot, which is the lenient direction. Frames 405 and 410 look at the stove and are genuinely out. (2) The stretch t=15-32 has the wearer handling a phone, a white card and something in the bathroom -- none of it this keyring, which is on the desk the whole time. If any of that is actually this object the middle of the file is wrong.
Event times use one rule: `placed` is the first frame the object is at rest ON the surface (11.5 and 49.0), whether or not the hand has finished withdrawing, and `picked_up` is the first frame it leaves it (42.5). The same rule puts 120727_hi's placement at t=7.1.
